gaps.sentence: You ___ park here — the police tow cars away every morning.
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' expresses a rule you must not break: mustn't park.

gaps.sentence: The report ___ have been finished yesterday; the deadline was missed.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have been finished' — it was expected but did not happen.

gaps.sentence: ___ I use your phone for a local call?
He ___ have missed the train — he left home two hours early.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' expresses near-certainty that something did not happen: can't have missed.

gaps.sentence: I really ___ stop drinking so much coffee; the doctor was very clear.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' can express strong obligation the speaker feels: must stop.

gaps.sentence: Candidates ___ switch off their phones before the exam begins.
I'm afraid you ___ smoke anywhere in the terminal; it is strictly forbidden.
This bill ___ be right — we only ordered two coffees.
gaps.hint: an obvious mistake, so it is impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' shows the speaker believes something is not possible: can't be right.
